body:
The drain was looping on held PRs — I pulled four out of the batch to stop it. Your merges are now the only path for those, and BUG-1447 is worse than I filed it

WHAT WAS HAPPENING. TASK-1298's PR-2014 was refused at 14:29:15 and again at 14:40:06 — shelve, requeue, re-attempt, refuse, shelve. Both retries burned each cycle. BUG-1310's PR-2016 the same at 14:35. The drain had started spending the night re-attempting merges it cannot perform.

I removed four specs from batch night-0920 so it stops picking them up:

  BUG-1297    PR #2006
  BUG-1310    PR #2016
  STORY-1350  PR #1974
  TASK-1298   PR #2014

That is dispatch, not disposition — their work is done and sitting in a PR; what they need is your merge, not another drive. Batch is at 10 and the drain has real work again. Say the word if you would rather they stayed in.

THE SCOPE FINDING, which I have put on BUG-1447. I checked `merge-hold-gate` across every open PR:

  12 held out of 12 open

So there is currently no open PR the drain can merge. The retry burn is not an occasional misclassification, it is phase 4's default outcome. That moves BUG-1447's criterion 2 from tidiness to the thing that stops the shelve log filling with false `tool-exit` records beside genuine ones.

ONE QUESTION I COULD NOT ANSWER, and it decides where the fix belongs. Drive-mode specs are held BY THE DRAIN so that a human merges them. If that is why these are held, then the drain attempting the merge at all is a second defect upstream of the classification — it is trying to merge something it deliberately gated. That is the difference between fixing phase 4's entry and fixing `is_merge_conflict_failure`. The answer is in the hold provenance and you have it; I do not.

AND THE PART I WOULD NOT HAVE PREDICTED. This defect existed all along and could not fire while your holds were marker-only. Enforcing them properly this morning is what exposed it. That is the second time tonight that fixing a gate revealed something the broken gate had been hiding — the first was #1983's ownership binding, where the guard that would have stopped a merge-over-live-drive was the one being held.

I am not drawing a moral about holds. The holds have been right. It is worth noticing that a gate which does not fire produces no evidence that it is needed, so its absence is invisible in exactly the way its presence is not.
